claim: For the labeled \(n\)-state Wielandt automaton \(W_n\) on \(Q=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\), where \(b(i)=i+1\pmod n\), \(c(0)=c(1)=2\), and \(c(i)=i+1\pmod n\) for \(2\le i<n\), let \(\lambda_n(s)=\min\{|w|:|Qw|\le n-s\}\). For every \(n\ge3\) and \(1\le s\le\lceil n/2\rceil\), \(\lambda_n(s)=2s-1\), and the unique word of that minimum length attaining rank at most \(n-s\) is \(c(bc)^{s-1}\). Moreover, when \(n\ge4\) and \(s_0=\lceil n/2\rceil\), the next threshold is strictly larger than the counting lower bound: \(\lambda_n(s_0+1)>2s_0+1\).

correctness.rationale: The lower bound follows because only \(c\) can decrease rank, each \(c\) lowers rank by at most one, and after an effective \(c\) state \(1\) is absent, forcing at least one \(b\) before the next effective \(c\). Equality therefore forces the unique pattern \(c(bc)^{s-1}\). A missing-state induction proves every \(c\) in that word is effective through \(\lceil n/2\rceil\), and a parity-specific image calculation shows the next \(c\) is ineffective. The included power-automaton replay independently confirms the full claimed regime for \(3\le n\le14\).

value.rationale: The Wielandt automata are a classical extremal family with quadratic reset threshold. Determining the exact initial rank-compression profile, the unique optimal words, and the exact point where the universal counting lower bound stops being tight isolates a structural feature of that family: its slow synchronization is not caused by slow initial loss of rank. This is a natural all-parameter invariant rather than a finite or ad hoc slice.
